title: Reconstituting Cytoarchitecture and Function of Human Epithelial Tissues on an Open-Top Organ-Chip
protocol: Place the crosslinker and solvent buffer reagents under the biosafety cabinet (BSC) and let them equilibrate at room temperature (RT) for 10 min before use.

Reconstitute 5 mg of crosslinker in 5 mL of the solvent buffer using a sterile light-impervious container or a transparent 15 mL conical tube wrapped in aluminum foil to protect the crosslinker solution from direct light exposure.
Vortex the solution for 1 min to remove all clumps, and then pipette 50 µL of the crosslinker solution directly into the bottom channel of the chip and 150 µL into the open-top chamber.
Remove any excess of crosslinking solution from the surface of the chip using an aspirator.
Pipette additional 50 µL of the crosslinking solution directly into the bottom channel of the chip and 150 µL into the open-top chamber to remove any remaining air bubble.
Gently remove the lid from the chip under the BSC and store it in a sterile container.
Transfer the chips containing the crosslinker solution into a Petri dish, close the Petri dish to avoid contamination, and place the dish with the chips under the UV crosslinking machine.
Remove the Petri dish lid to maximize the UV exposure.
Set the UV crosslinking machine with a peak wavelength of 365 nm at an intensity of 100 µJ/cm².
Turn on the UV light for 20 min.
Aspirate the oxidized crosslinker solution after 20 min of UV treatment.
Rinse all chips three times with solvent buffer.
Let the chips dry under the BSC for 5-10 min.
Dissolve 2.2 g of sodium bicarbonate in 75 mL of 0.067 M NaOH in double-distilled water.
Add 4.76 g of HEPES to the solution.
Bring the volume to 100 mL using double distilled water.
Sterile filter the solution under the BSC using a disposable sterile bottle-top filter with a 0.22 µm membrane.
Multiply the number of chips needed for the experiment by 150 µL to estimate the amount of pre-gel solution required.
Prepare the collagen pre-gel solution on ice by mixing 1 volume of 10x EMEM containing cells, 1 volume of 10x reconstruction buffer, and 8 volumes of collagen I solution (10 mg/mL).
Add 1 µL of 1 N NaOH solution for each mg of collagen I.
Bring the following solutions under the BSC on ice: 10x EMEM; 10x Reconstruction buffer; Collagen I solution (10 mg/mL); and Sterile 1 N NaOH solution.
Dissociate tissue-specific mesenchymal cells using trypsin or other methods recommended by the cell provider once they reach 80%-90% confluence.
Collect the cells in a pellet by centrifugation at 250 x g for 5 min at 24°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 225 µL of ice-cold 10x EMEM.
Add 225 µL of ice-cold 10x reconstruction buffer to the resuspended cells.
Mix the solution by gently pipetting up and down.
Add 1,800 µL of ice-cold collagen I solution to the mixed cell suspension.
Pipette up and down 5-6 times to mix the pre-gel solution while on ice.
Neutralize the pre-gel solution with 18 µL of 1 N NaOH.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down 5-6 times.
Pipette 150 µL of cell-laden hydrogel into the central chamber of the Open-Top Chip avoiding bubbles.
Group the chips into separate Petri dishes.
Place a centrifuge tube cap filled with 2 mL of sterile ddH2O in each Petri dish.
Incubate the Petri dishes at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 90 min.
Remove any residue of the hydrogel that may spill from the top of the open-top chamber using an aspirator.
Coat the vascular microfluidic chamber with extracellular matrix proteins.
Estimate the volume of vascular ECM coating solution required by multiplying the number of chips needed for the experiment by 20 μL.
Prepare an extra 15% volume to account for experimental errors.
Prepare the vascular ECM coating solution using ice-cold PBS or HBSS.
Pipette 20 µL of vascular ECM coating solution into the vascular channel of each chip.
Estimate the volume of epithelial ECM coating solution required by multiplying the number of chips needed for the experiment by 50 μL.
Prepare an extra 15% volume to account for experimental errors.
Prepare enough ECM coating solution in ice-cold PBS or HBSS.
Transfer 50 µL of epithelial ECM coating solution directly on top of the hydrogel surface.
Culture tissue-specific epithelial cells as directed by the providers until 80%-90% confluent.
Dissociate the cells using proteolytic enzyme procedures as recommended by the cell provider.
Harvest epithelial cells at low passage (P1-P2) during the active growth phase when they reach between 70%-90% confluency.
Centrifuge the cells and collect them as a pellet.
Resuspend the epithelial cells to the appropriate cell/fragment density as indicated in the specific organ protocol table.
Transfer the chips from the incubator into the BSC.
Aspirate the coating solution from the vascular channel.
Rinse the vascular microfluidic channel three times with 50 µL of fresh endothelial cell culture medium.
Aspirate the coating solution from the hydrogel surface.
Rinse the stromal surface three times with 100 µL of fresh epithelial cell culture medium to remove any excess coating solution.
Aspirate the rinsing medium.
Seed the hydrogel surface with 50 µL of the epithelial cell suspension using appropriate cell density, as indicated in the supplementary tables.
Transfer the chips back into the incubator for 2 h (or overnight for colonoids).
Gently rinse the hydrogel surface with the cell culture medium twice to remove cellular debris.
Refresh the medium by autoclaving in sealed autoclavable containers.
Connect the chips to the peristaltic pump.
Cut 2 inches of biocompatible polypropylene-based thermoplastic elastomer (TPE) transfer tubing for short microfluidic tubing.
Cut 7.5 inches of biocompatible TPE transfer tubing for long microfluidic tubing.
Prepare enough 18 G and 19 G metal connectors.
Allow the cell culture medium to equilibrate to room temperature (RT).
Transfer the volume of medium needed into a conical filtering tube.
Apply a negative vacuum pressure of -20 PSI to degas the medium (vacuum-driven filtration).
Pipette 200 µL of the degassed cell culture medium into the inlet port of both the top and bottom channels of the chip while paying attention to avoid bubbles.
Pipette 300 µL of the culture medium into the short microfluidic tubing to prime the inner surface of the tubes.
Connect the short tubing to the inlets of the top and bottom channels of the chip.
Position the medium reservoirs into the farm rack.
Connect the hypodermic needle to the bottom inlet of the chips.
Accommodate all the chips in the housing carrier(s) inside the incubator.
Connect the chips to the peristaltic pump.
Inspect all connectors for proper connection and no visible leakage.
Use the Purge button on the pump and hold it for about 15 s or until droplets of cell culture medium appear at the end of the outflow tubing.
Set the appropriate organ-chip flow rate using the control system on the pump.
Prepare fresh cell culture medium for the epithelium and/or endothelium, and perform degassing steps.
Pause the peristaltic pump.
Carefully disconnect the chips from the pump.
Extract the chip housing carrier(s).
Transfer the chips from the incubator to the BSC.
Remove the volume of media left in the reservoirs.
Replace cell culture media in the top and bottom inlet reservoirs with 5 mL of fresh medium.
Place the chip housing carrier(s) back into the incubator.
Connect the chips to the peristaltic pump.
Restart the flow.
Use the Purge function to rapidly refresh the medium to the vascular compartment.
Pause the peristaltic pump.
Disconnect chips from the pump and extract chip housing carrier(s).
Transfer chips from the incubator to the biosafety cabinet.
Remove medium left in top reservoir of the chip.
Gently aspirate all medium from the top microfluidic channel.
Clamp short microfluidic tubing connected to top inlets using binder clips.
Place Open-Top Chip on housing carrier(s) back into the incubator and reconnect chips to the peristaltic pump.
Connect vacuum ports of chips to vacuum module using long microfluidic tubes per chip.
Adjust stretch setting using vacuum module as specified inside organ protocol tables.
Visually inspect tube connections for proper chip connection and absence of medium droplets.
Resume the flow by starting the peristaltic pump.
Culture tissue-specific endothelial cells until they reach 80%-90% confluence.
Dissociate the cells using a proteolytic enzyme procedure as recommended by the provider.
Resuspend the endothelial cells in a solution of 3 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Pause the peristaltic pump.
Transfer chips from the incubator to the BSC.
Disconnect chips from media reservoirs and any connected tubing.
Group chips into separate Petri dishes.
Refresh cell culture medium of the epithelial compartment with fresh epithelial cell culture medium.
Rinse vascular channel with fresh endothelium cell culture medium twice.
Aspirate the medium from the vascular compartment.
Seed the bottom (vascular) channel with 25 µL of endothelial cell suspension (3 x 10^6 cells/mL).
Flip chips upside down to allow endothelial cells to attach to the upper surface of the microfluidic chamber.
Place chips back into the incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Let endothelial cells attach for 1 hour.
Transfer the chips from the incubator to the BSC after 1 hour.
Rinse the vascular channel with endothelial cell culture medium twice to remove cellular debris.
Seed the vascular channel again with endothelial cells as per steps 8.2.1-8.2.2.
Lay the chips flat to facilitate adhesion of endothelial cells to the bottom surface of the vascular channel.
Fill up the vascular medium reservoir with degassed vascular cell culture medium under the BSC.
Reconnect the chip to flow by connecting one end to a peristaltic pump and the other to the medium reservoirs.
Use the Purge function to rapidly refresh the medium in the vascular compartment and reduce air bubble risk.
Inspect microfluidic connections visually to ensure proper connection with no visible droplets of medium dripping.
Resume fluid flow by starting the peristaltic pump after visual inspection is complete.
Pause the peristaltic pump when preparing for endpoint assays.
Disconnect chips from the pump carefully and extract chip housing carrier(s).
Transfer chip housing carrier(s) from incubator to BSC and set chips free.
Gently wash the central chamber of the Open-Top Chip with epithelial cell culture medium twice.
Wash the vascular channel with endothelium culture medium twice to remove cellular debris.
Remove the lid of the Open-Top Chip to access the apical compartment using tweezers.
Proceed with conventional sample fixation, permeabilization, and blocking.
Fix samples in 200 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 1 h followed by rinsing with PBS.
Permeabilize samples in 0.1% Triton X-100 for 40 min.
Block samples in 1% bovine serum albumin for 1 h.
Incubate the chips with primary antibodies at 4 °C overnight.
Wash both epithelial and endothelial compartments of the chip with 200 µL of PBS twice.
Proceed with secondary antibodies for 2 h.
Dilute primary antibodies in PBS + 1% BSA at a dilution of 1:100.
Dilute secondary antibodies in PBS + 1% BSA at a dilution of 1:200.
Extract the stromal equivalents from the main chamber using tweezers.
Collect stromal equivalents into a 1.5 mL tube filled with 10% neutral buffered formalin.
Incubate for at least 24 h.
Transfer the fixed stromal equivalent to the tissue processor.
Submerge the hydrogel in 70% ethanol for 90 min.
Remove and submerge the hydrogel in 80% ethanol for 90 min.
Remove and submerge the hydrogel in 95% ethanol for 90 min.
Remove and submerge the hydrogel in 100% ethanol for 90 min twice.
Remove 100% ethanol from the hydrogel.
Submerge the hydrogel in xylene for 120 min twice.
Infiltrate the stromal equivalents in paraffin wax for 120 min (~2 h) twice.
Embed the infiltrated stromal equivalents into sectioning paraffin blocks.
Section the embedded stromal equivalents using a microtome.
